tasks.short: Count food supplies and check equipment, enter counts, work out stock differences and report damage or big gaps to the kitchen manager.

steps.what: Cook counts food supplies in stores, fridges and freezers: on a paper count sheet today, on a tablet in shelf order after the change
Cook checks kitchen equipment and small wares for damage and missing items
Cook types the counts into the stock spreadsheet
Cook works out stock values and differences against deliveries and use
Cook reports damaged equipment and large stock gaps to the kitchen manager

tasks.design: Counts are entered on a tablet in the kitchen management system ({OTHER}), with items listed in the order they sit on the shelves, so they land in the stock record directly. The system values stock at current supplier prices and shows the difference from deliveries minus recorded use; checking equipment and talking to the manager stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts were written on paper, typed into a spreadsheet and compared by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Kitchen software links recipes and ingredients to supplier prices, so stock can be valued and use derived.
tasks.still_hard: Counting is still physical; differences only make sense if deliveries and use are recorded.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that a gap is a broken delivery, not theft or waste.

reach.learn: Whether valued stock counts sharpen monthly food cost.

evidence.claim: Kitchen recipe software links recipes to supplier prices so costs follow price changes.
Kitchen stock apps take counts on tablets in storage order.

assumptions: Boundary: from counting to reporting; ordering is outside.
Input contract: item list and storage order kept by the kitchen manager; supplier prices from the supplier's price file; deliveries booked by the cook on receipt; fallback is the paper sheet.
Counts are recorded per kitchen, not per cook.

Equipment checks and reporting keep their full time. s1 keeps 85 because shelf order saves some walking and the count itself stays; typing the counts goes; s4 keeps 30 for reading and checking the difference list.
unknowns: Whether deliveries are booked in a system today.
research_questions: Do stock differences shrink once use is recorded?

already_counted.description: Cook checks the difference list before reporting.

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: learning the tablet count screen is a one-off.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: deliveries and use are not booked, so no difference list appears and only typing goes (25.0); high: deliveries booked on receipt as assumed (36.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Estimate future needs from menus and numbers, compare with stock, order food, request equipment, get approval and pass it to purchasing.

steps.what: Cook estimates future needs from the menu cycle and expected numbers of patients or pupils
Cook compares the needs with stock on hand
Cook reviews the proposed food order
Cook checks the final food order: lines, quantities, delivery dates and the supplier it goes to
Cook sends the checked food order to the supplier: by phone or e-mail today, through the supplier's ordering portal after the change
Cook writes requisitions for kitchen equipment and appliances with reason and price
Kitchen manager checks the equipment requisition: item, reason, price and budget
Kitchen manager approves the checked requisition, which routes it to purchasing
Cook takes the signed requisition form to purchasing and follows it up today; after the change the form routes there and the cook only follows up delays

tasks.design: The kitchen management system ({OTHER}) turns the menu cycle and expected numbers into quantities per ingredient from house recipes, subtracts stock, and proposes an order that the cook adjusts, checks and sends to the supplier's ordering portal. Equipment requests are a form in {PROCUREMENT} that routes to the kitchen manager, who checks it and approves it, which sends it on to purchasing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Needs were estimated from memory and spreadsheets, and requisitions were paper forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Kitchen software links recipes to ingredients and supplier prices, and production forecasts per service exist in kitchen tools.
tasks.still_hard: Numbers change with admissions and school events; the cook adjusts every proposal.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing that next week's heat means more cold dishes and less soup.
tasks.altitude: The cook adjusts proposed orders; approval of equipment stays with the kitchen manager.

reach.learn: Whether routed forms cut follow-up calls.

evidence.claim: Kitchen recipe software links recipes to supplier prices so costs follow price changes.
A kitchen waste tool also forecasts production per service.
No high-risk AI category covers ordering or menus; this design uses no model.

assumptions: Boundary: from estimating needs to requests at suppliers and purchasing; receiving is outside.

Input contract: expected numbers from the ward or school administration; stock record kept by the cooks' counts; house recipes kept by the head cook; supplier catalogue from the supplier's portal; fallback is paper and phone.
Kitchen manager and purchasing time is outside the cook's savings. The cook's order check keeps its full time; sending keeps 25; s6 keeps 20 for following up delays.
Food orders within par levels need no approval.
research_questions: Do proposed orders cut over-ordering and waste?

already_counted.description: Cook checks the proposed supplier order.

incremental.description: Cook enters expected numbers when the administration sends them.
Head cook keeps recipe quantities current.

approvals.approved_version: The equipment requisition with item, reason and price exactly as checked by the kitchen manager in s5, approved once in s5r and routed to purchasing; any change needs a new check and approval.
The food order with lines, quantities and delivery dates exactly as checked by the cook in s7c, sent once to the supplier's ordering portal; changes after that need a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: expected numbers change often and several suppliers take orders only by phone (41.9); high: stable numbers and portal suppliers (54.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check commodity deliveries, watch storage and use, log use per meal, reconcile stock, prepare the monthly report and have it submitted.

steps.what: Cook checks government food commodities delivered against the allocation list
Cook watches that commodities are stored, rotated and used under the proper procedures
Cook records what was produced for each eligible meal in the kitchen management system
Cook logs commodity use per meal on paper usage sheets
Cook reconciles commodity stock with the usage log each month
Cook fills in the monthly commodity report
Kitchen manager checks and signs the commodity report: quantities received, used and on hand against the records, and the agency it goes to
Kitchen manager submits the report to the agency

tasks.design: Commodity items are flagged in the kitchen management system ({OTHER}); deliveries are booked against the allocation, and use is derived from the recipes produced for eligible meals, for the cook to confirm. The monthly reconciliation and report are built from those records; watching storage and use, and the manager's submission, stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Use was logged on paper sheets and the report was compiled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Kitchen software links each recipe to its ingredients, so use can be derived from production.
tasks.still_hard: Derived use is only right if production is recorded; rules differ per programme.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting that commodity food is going to the wrong meals before an audit does.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; logging and arithmetic shrink.

reach.task: Report commodity use to the agency
reach.learn: Whether derived use passes programme audits.

evidence.claim: Kitchen recipe software links each recipe to its ingredients and supplier prices.
Government food programmes require records of receipt, use and stock per commodity.

assumptions: Boundary: from commodity delivery to the report submitted; programme applications are outside.
Input contract: allocation lists from the programme agency; commodity flags and eligible meals set by the kitchen manager; production recorded by the cooks; fallback is paper sheets.
Kitchen manager time is outside the cook's savings.

Watching storage and use and recording production (s3p, a first record) keep their full time. s1 keeps 60 because deliveries are booked against the allocation and the physical check stays; s3 keeps 30 for confirming derived use; s4 keeps 30 and s5 keeps 40 for checking.
unknowns: Which programmes the kitchen takes part in.
research_questions: Does derived use match counted stock closely enough for audits?

already_counted.description: Cook confirms derived use per meal.
Cook checks the reconciliation before the report.

incremental.description: Kitchen manager keeps commodity flags and eligible meals current.
No ongoing upkeep beyond the steps: recording production is shown in s3p.

approvals.approved_version: The commodity report as signed by the kitchen manager in s6.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: production is not recorded for many meals, so use is still logged on paper (29.3); high: production recorded for eligible meals (36.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather feedback, diets and season, draft cycle menus, check nutrition and allergens, cost them, get dietitian approval and publish.

steps.what: Cook reviews meal feedback, diet categories and foods in season
Cook drafts varied cycle menus from house recipes

loop.input: House recipe base with nutrition, allergen and cost per portion, the season list from the produce supplier, diet categories with counts (no names) and last cycle's feedback.
loop.output: A four-week cycle menu built only from house recipes, with a diet alternative for each meal.
loop.check: Code rejects the draft if any dish is not in the recipe base, a diet category lacks a safe alternative by the recipes' allergen fields, daily nutrient targets are missed, cost per meal exceeds the cap, or a dish repeats within 14 days; the cook then reads the passing draft for appeal and balance.
loop.stop: Stop when all rules pass; after three failed drafts the cook plans that week by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Choosing an appealing, seasonal mix under many constraints is a search that fixed rules cannot write; rules can only check it.

steps.what: Cook checks the nutritionally balanced targets and allergens per dish with tables
Cook costs the menu against the budget per meal
Dietitian approves the cycle menu for patient diets
Cook checks the menu before publishing: it is the version the dietitian approved, and the wards and meal ordering system it goes to
Cook publishes the menu to wards and the meal ordering system

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts a four-week cycle menu from the house recipe base in the kitchen management system ({OTHER}), and code rejects any draft that breaks diet, nutrient, cost or repeat rules. Nutrition, allergens and cost come from ingredient data, never from the model; the dietitian approves, and the cook checks the approved version and publishes it to the wards and the meal ordering system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Menus were planned in spreadsheets and checked against tables by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Kitchen software carries allergen and nutrition data per ingredient into every recipe and menu, and language models can propose combinations that code then checks.
tasks.still_hard: Appeal and variety are taste judgements; allergen data are only as good as the supplier specifications.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what residents will actually eat and making the menu feel like home.

ambition.what: Menus replanned each season from feedback and local produce instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The cook chooses among checked drafts; the dietitian keeps approval of patient diets.

reach.learn: Whether the same rules suit school nutrition targets.

evidence.claim: Kitchen recipe software carries allergen and nutrition data per ingredient into every recipe and menu.
A menu tool detects the 14 EU allergens on a menu, and its healthcare module hides dishes a resident may not eat.
Allergen information is mandatory for non-prepacked food and the operator stays responsible for its accuracy.
Diet restrictions can reveal health or religion and are special-category data.

assumptions: Boundary: from feedback to the published menu; cooking is outside.

Input contract: house recipes with ingredient specifications kept by the head cook; nutrient targets and diet rules set by the dietitian; season list from the produce supplier; diet counts from the ward administration without names; fallback is planning by hand.
Dietitian time is outside the cook's savings.
No allergen statement comes from the model.

Reviewing feedback and the check before publishing keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because drafts meet the rules and the cook still reads them for appeal and balance and swaps dishes; s3 keeps 25 for confirming flagged results; costing goes because it comes from ingredient data; publishing keeps 50.
unknowns: How many diet categories the kitchen serves.
research_questions: Does plate waste fall with menus replanned each season?

already_counted.description: Cook reads the passing draft for appeal and balance.
Cook confirms flagged nutrition and allergen results.

incremental.description: Cook enters new recipes with full ingredient data.
Dietitian keeps nutrient targets and diet rules current.

approvals.approved_version: The cycle menu version approved by the dietitian in s5 and checked by the cook in s6c, published once to the wards and the meal ordering system; any dish swap needs a new approval and check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: recipe data are incomplete, so many dishes are checked and costed by hand and drafts need much rework (27.8); high: complete recipe data (54.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The institution cook keeps cooking, tasting and judgement on menus; counting, ordering arithmetic and logs move to the kitchen system.
skills_to_grow: Keeping recipe and ingredient data complete
role.ambitious_version: A cook who replans menus every season from what residents eat, with paperwork that writes itself from the kitchen's records.
